title: Does money matter in the euro area? Evidence from a new Divisia index
abstract: We create a euro-area Divisia-money dataset and estimate theoretically correct responses to money, user cost and interest rate shocks using structural vector-autoregressions. Our findings suggest that money matters for output, prices and interest rates, while the European Central Bank can influence monetary developments.
summary_en: Standard 'simple-sum' monetary aggregates (M1, M2, M3) treat all components as perfect substitutes — a clearly wrong assumption. Divisia indices weight components by their user costs, producing theoretically correct measures. Darvas constructs a euro-area Divisia-money series and estimates structural-VAR responses to money, user-cost, and interest-rate shocks. The findings: money does matter for euro-area output, prices, and interest rates; ECB monetary policy can influence monetary developments. The result revives the case for monitoring money in ECB analysis.
data_used: Euro-area monetary statistics from ECB Statistical Data Warehouse, decomposed into Divisia-money components with user-cost weights; structural VAR over multiple decades of euro-area data.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for MNB monetary-aggregates analysis and for the ECB's monetary-pillar discussions. The paper supports the use of Divisia-money series as a complement to standard monetary aggregates in macroeconomic forecasting and policy analysis. Useful for MNB methodology and Hungarian Government euro-area discussions.
